precepts.why:
“Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe; over Philistia will I triumph.” God says Moab is going to wash our clothes; they will be our laundromat forever. And he casts his shoe over Edom. That is why we are not supposed to be married to them. God says come out from among them and be ye separate. Some of us come of mixed parentage, and that is fine, but find yourself an Israelite woman, an Israelite man, and don't do this no more.

Isaiah shows the same triumph: “But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west; they shall spoil them of the east together.” We shall fly upon the shoulders of the Palestinians toward the west, and we shall spoil them of the east together.

“they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.” We shall lay our hands upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon, the Japanese, shall obey us.

So the nations that rule over Israel now, Edom, Moab and Ammon, will be under Israel's hand. That is what God means when he calls Moab his washpot and casts his shoe over Edom: they will serve.

precepts.text: I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border. You think they love us? God says they reproach us; they hate us. Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah: that has not happened yet. And the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. Nobody escapes what they did to God's chosen people. And with that we say: twelve tribes.

precepts.why:
God calls Moab his washpot, and Zephaniah shows why Moab and Ammon come to that end: “I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border.”

God says, I heard what them damn Chinese said about my people, and the hatred of the Japanese. You think they love us? God says they reproach us; they hate us. They magnified themselves against the Israelites.

“Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation.” Destruction upon the earth: that is nuclear fire, and it has not happened yet.

“the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.” The remnant of God's people shall spoil them, put them into captivity, and possess them; they are going to serve us. Nobody escapes, brothers and sisters. Nobody gets away with what they did to God's chosen people. And with that we say: twelve tribes.

precepts.text: Israel is the beloved of the Bible, and this is our God, the God of our forefathers.
precepts.point: Moab is His washpot, the servant, and over Edom He casts out His shoe, treating Edom as a slave to clean His shoes.
precepts.why:
“That thy beloved may be delivered”. Baruch tells who the beloved is: “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

Israel is the beloved of the Bible. And this is our God, the God of our forefathers, who found out all the way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his servant. So the deliverance David prays for is the deliverance of Israel.

precepts.text: According to His name, so is His praise unto the ends of the earth; His right hand is full of righteousness.
precepts.point: Moab is His washpot, the servant, and over Edom He casts out His shoe, treating Edom as a slave to clean His shoes.
precepts.why:
“save with thy right hand, and answer me.” Psalm 48 shows what the right hand is: “According to thy name, O God, so is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of righteousness.”

His right hand is full of righteousness, so the Israelites, his beloved, will be saved by keeping God's commandments. That is the saving with the right hand that David asks for.

precepts.text: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah nor a lawgiver from between his feet until Shiloh come, the prophecy of Christ, unto whom the gathering of the people shall be.
precepts.point: Moab is His washpot, the servant, and over Edom He casts out His shoe, treating Edom as a slave to clean His shoes.
precepts.why:
“Judah is my lawgiver”. That goes back to Jacob's blessing: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

Judah being the lawgiver is a prophecy of Christ, from whom the sceptre and the rulership shall not depart, and unto whom the gathering of the people shall be. God has spoken in his holiness: Gilead is his, Manasseh is his, Ephraim is the strength of his head, and Judah is his lawgiver.

points: O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise even with my glory. Awake, psaltery and harp; I myself will awake early. We are to be singing praise to the Lord all the time amongst the nations, letting your light shine.

I will praise thee among the people and sing praises unto thee among the nations, for thy mercy is great above the heavens and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds. Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory above all the earth.

That thy beloved may be delivered, save with thy right hand and answer me. The beloved is Israel, and the right hand is full of righteousness, so the Israelites will be saved by keeping God's commandments.

God has spoken in His holiness: Gilead is His, Manasseh is His, Ephraim is the strength of His head, and Judah is His lawgiver. Judah being the lawgiver is a prophecy of Christ, from whom the sceptre and rulership shall not depart.
Moab is His washpot, the servant, and over Edom He casts out His shoe, treating Edom as a slave to clean His shoes.

Who will bring me into the strong city, who will lead me into Edom? Wilt not thou, O God, who hadst cast us off, and wilt not thou go forth with our hosts? We must call upon the name of the Lord to give us help from trouble, and the trouble is our enemies.
Give us help from trouble, for vain is the help of man. Through God we shall do valiantly, for it is He that shall tread down our enemies.
